claims.text: Conventional thermomechanical processing can produce a uniform microstructure with high strength but reduced ductility.
SMAT produces severe plastic deformation at the material surface.
SMAT followed by controlled annealing can create a smooth surface-to-core gradient in grain size.
SMAT followed by controlled annealing can create a smooth surface-to-core gradient in phase distribution.
The resulting outer layer contains nano- to ultrafine grains.
The refined outer layer gradually transitions to a coarser core.
The coarser core retains high strength.
A gradient microstructure delays tensile necking.
The gradient microstructure accommodates plasticity at the surface while the core maintains high strength.
Spatial tailoring of the microstructure distributes tensile strain more broadly.
More distributed strain balances dislocation motion and delays failure.
Introducing the proposed gradient microstructure can overcome the conventional strength–ductility trade-off.
Relative to a uniformly processed material, the gradient-treated material will exhibit greater elongation to failure.
Relative to a uniformly processed material, the gradient-treated material will retain or slightly increase yield strength and ultimate tensile strength.
The proposed improvement is limited to alloys amenable to SMAT and controlled annealing.
Excessive grain coarsening or degradation of the gradient may prevent the proposed strength–ductility improvement.
The magnitude of strengthening and ductility enhancement depends on alloy composition, SMAT intensity, and annealing profile.
